title: Fix pacman error: target not found when installing a package
summary: pacman says 'target not found' when the package name you typed is not in its package list. Find the exact name, refresh the list with a full upgrade, then run the install again.

aliases.text: pacman error target not found arch
arch linux pacman package not found
arch linux pacman не могу найти пакет
pacman установка ошибка target not found

prerequisites: Arch Linux with an internet connection
An account that is allowed to use sudo (an administrator account)

steps.explain: Search the package list for a word from the program name. The exact name is the part after the slash, for example nano in core/nano. This command only reads the list.

placeholders.name: SEARCH_WORD
placeholders.description: A word from the name of the program you want

steps.expect: Lines like 'core/nano 9.2-1', each followed by a short description. The part after the slash (nano) is the exact name. No lines means no package matches the word.

steps.explain: Check that the exact name exists. pacman -Si prints the details of one package name and only reads the list.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Exact package name copied from the search result

steps.expect: Lines starting with 'Repository' and 'Name', for example 'Name : nano'. If you see "error: package '<PACKAGE>' was not found", the name is wrong: go back to the search and copy the name exactly.

steps.explain: Refresh the package list on this computer, which may be old. This also upgrades installed programs, so it takes a while. Do not use pacman -Sy alone, because that can break Arch.
steps.expect: sudo asks for your password. pacman prints ':: Synchronizing package databases...', then the packages to upgrade and 'Proceed with installation? [Y/n]'. Type y and press Enter.

steps.explain: Install the package by its exact name. Use the name that the previous steps confirmed. Replace <PACKAGE> with it.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Exact package name confirmed by pacman -Si

steps.expect: pacman lists the package and asks 'Proceed with installation? [Y/n]'. Type y and press Enter. 'error: target not found: <PACKAGE>' means the name is still not in the Arch repositories.

steps.explain: Check that the package is installed. pacman -Q prints the installed name and version and only reads the list.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Same package name as in the install step

steps.expect: The name and version, for example 'nano 9.2-1'. If you see "error: package '<PACKAGE>' was not found", the install did not finish.

rollback.explain: Remove the package again if you installed the wrong one. This removes only that package. It does not undo the upgrade from the refresh step.

placeholders.name: PACKAGE
placeholders.description: Same package name as in the install step

warnings: sudo pacman -Syu upgrades every installed package and can take a long time. Do not interrupt it, because a half-finished upgrade can break the system.
Do not run pacman -Sy alone and then install. Refreshing the list without upgrading the system leaves Arch in a partly updated state. Always use -Syu.
Type your password only when sudo asks for it, and read the package list before you answer y.
If sudo says 'is not in the sudoers file', your account cannot use sudo. Ask the owner of the computer to add it.
A wrong name gives 'target not found' and nothing is installed. Copy the name from the search exactly, including dashes.
